decisions.quote:
N400 amplitude reductions observed to both semantically/associatively- and orthographically-related words indicate that at a reading rate of two words per second, word forms as well as semantic features are preactivated, at least in highly constraining sentence contexts. These results contrast with those of
Ito et al. (2016)
, who did not observe N400 amplitude reductions to form-related words at the same moderate presentation rate.
decisions.reason: The central finding this replication was designed to test (and the focus of its title) is Ito et al. (2016)'s finding that word form preactivation does not occur at a 500 ms SOA (two words per second); finding a significant form-related N400 reduction where the original found none is coded as failed, and the authors also note (lines 600-602) that their posterior PNP pattern differed from Ito et al. (2016) while concluding overall against Ito et al.'s time-constraint proposal.
